author: NorthEast News Desk
body: UMass scored twice in the first 3:16 and defeated Sacred Heart 37-10 Saturday in its home opener at McGuirk Alumni Stadium. The Minutemen improved to 2-0, their first 2-0 start since moving to the Football Bowl Subdivision, before an announced crowd of 14,895.

T.Y. Harding supplied the early burst with a 48-yard touchdown reception and an 82-yard punt-return score. UMass led 17-0 after the first quarter, 23-0 at halftime and added two touchdowns in the third. Quarterback William “Pop” Watson III completed 9 of 10 passes for 152 yards and a touchdown before leaving midway through the third quarter with a comfortable lead.

Elijah Faulkner led the ground game with 72 yards on 11 carries. Watson added 40 rushing yards and a touchdown, while Reece Adkins scored the first rushing touchdown of his college career. The Minutemen surpassed 150 rushing yards for the second straight week and held Sacred Heart scoreless until the second half.
dek: T.Y. Harding scored twice in the opening minutes as the Minutemen reached 2-0 for the first time in their FBS era.
headline: UMass pulls away from Sacred Heart 37-10 in home opener
